name: rsi_reversal_v1
author: claude_strategist
mechanism: On NIFTY, sharp 2-minute directional moves push RSI(24) into extreme territory (<30 or >70) as stop-loss cascades or momentum-chasing algos overshoot fair value. When this exhaustion occurs while the index is displaced from its 30-minute EMA — meaning price has deviated from where VWAP-benchmarked institutional algorithms are anchored — market makers absorb the terminal flow and resting limit orders accumulate. Within 30-90 seconds, the overshoot reverses as VWAP-tracking algorithms and gamma-hedging desks push the index back toward the 30-minute mean, creating a 10-20 spot point bounce (or fade) that option buyers can capture at ATM delta ~0.5.

indicators.name: rsi_24
indicators.purpose: 2-minute RSI to detect short-term exhaustion. NOT 14×12=168 blind scaling. The original 14-bar on 1-min measures 14 minutes of selling pressure. We are trading the FAST overshoot (first 30-90 seconds of reversion), not the slow multi-minute recovery — so the trigger must reflect recent 2-minute pressure, not 14-minute momentum. RSI(24) at 5-second bars = 2-minute window, which matches our hold time.

indicators.name: ema_360
indicators.purpose: 30-minute trend context as displacement anchor. The original EMA(200) on 1-min = 200-minute (3.3 hr) filter, which effectively measured whether you were above or below the full-session trend. For NIFTY intraday, a 30-minute EMA captures the current session direction without anchoring to pre-market open gaps. Trades where close < ema_360 with RSI<30 are buying dips back toward the intraday mean; trades where close > ema_360 with RSI>70 are fading extensions above intraday mean. This is the same logic as the original, compressed to the intraday regime.

buy_ce.confirmation: RSI turns from below oversold threshold while price is below the 30-min EMA — buying the fast reversion leg back toward intraday mean

buy_pe.confirmation: RSI in overbought zone while extended above 30-min EMA — fading the momentum overshoot as VWAP-benchmarked algos start selling

exit.stop_rationale: 4 option points (~8 spot pts at delta 0.5). If NIFTY continues to move against us by 8 spot pts beyond entry within 30 seconds, the stop-loss cascade has not exhausted and RSI can remain in extreme territory — the thesis is wrong. 8 spot pts is the threshold between 'overshoot' and 'trend continuation' on NIFTY at 2-minute timescales.
exit.target_rationale: 6 option points (~12 spot pts at delta 0.5). A 2-minute exhaustion reversion on NIFTY typically covers 15-25 spot pts. Targeting 12 spot pts captures 50-80% of the expected first leg reversion, giving 1:1.5 R:R with the stop at 4 pts. This is conservative enough to be hit within the 90-second time window.

filters.vix_filter: vix < 25 — same as original; above 25 RSI extremes on NIFTY are unreliable as panic selling can sustain RSI<20 for minutes
filters.time_filter: 09:20-15:25 IST; skip first 5 minutes (09:15-09:20) as RSI meaningless on first bars
filters.volume_filter: none — NIFTY index volume at 5s is noisy and not a reliable filter
filters.trend_filter: EMA(360) used as displacement anchor, not a strict trend direction filter
filters.spread_filter: none — limit order execution, no spread cost

edge.edge_decay_risk: medium — RSI reversion is well-known; edge depends on 5-second entry timing advantage vs 1-minute confirmation in original

adaptation_notes: Three key changes from the original equity strategy: (1) RSI period compressed from 14 to 24 bars — same 14-minute total lookback NOT applied; instead we target the 2-minute fast exhaustion signal that matches our 30-90s hold. (2) EMA period compressed from 200×1min to 360×5s (30 minutes) — capturing intraday trend context rather than the full-session 3.3-hour window of the original. (3) Stops/targets converted from percentage-based (0.2%/0.4% of spot) to fixed option premium points (4/6 pts) calibrated to typical NIFTY ATM option moves at 30-90s timescales. The directional logic is preserved: buy when RSI extreme AND price is on the 'wrong' side of the trend anchor, expecting reversion toward the mean.
weaknesses: RSI(24) at 5-second bars is sensitive to single large candles — one 10-pt NIFTY spike can push RSI to 90 without sustained trend
EMA(360) has 30-minute warmup; signals unreliable in first 30 minutes of session
Mean reversion fails during macro news events when NIFTY trends strongly in one direction — VIX filter partially mitigates but doesn't eliminate
Original win rate was only 0.45; at 5-second frequency with tighter stops, win rate may not improve significantly
